reviewed_by: claude, 2026-08-10: read every tile of the 6 pool sheets (runs/qc/greene_factory_v002/), the 2 wave-2 sheets, the 2 wave-3 sheets and the 1 wave-4 sheet, then re-read every tile of the 3 final sheets over the accepted pool. Every clip carried to acceptance was also checked on 4 frames spread across its length (runs/qc/greene_facecheck/facecheck_01..07.png, facecheck_w3.png), because the 1-second frame a contact sheet shows is not the clip.
note:
POOL REBUILT 2026-08-10. It held 9 clips against a floor of ~41 (31 min / 45 s). The v001 query set was written in a director's language ('front door house', 'moving boxes', 'empty room', 'paper', 'envelope') and 35 of its 47 clips were rejected on sight. The queries were rewritten in the SUPPLIER's vocabulary (config/episode_footage_queries.v001.json, 135 strings, each counted against the shelf before it was written): 'typewriter' returns 0 and the supplier's own misspelling 'old typwriter' returns the clip. 197 clips were staged across four waves; 51 are accepted, 9 clear of the floor.
Rejections fall into six kinds: an identifiable face (6, two of them clips the v001 review had ACCEPTED -- AR-6944084 a man's lit face, AR-8909763 a woman in profile with an infant); readable text or a surname/brand in frame (7); a register this film does not use -- graffiti and urban decay, demolition, money, courtroom, corporate glass, drone, nature (58); 3D renders and cartoons (9); a clip already burned in another episode, measured by content hash not filename (26); and portrait or below 1920x1080 (4). Neither of the last two is visible on a contact sheet.
Two clips are usable only in tight framing: AR-9306134 (the pin going into the corkboard is the footnote's thumbtack, but a finance chart sits behind it -- do not play it wide) and AR-v_45471 (the shut door and its threshold are the first seconds; the shot drifts into ivy after that).
notes: 2026-08-10: the shelf was searched with the factory ledger INCLUDED (shelf_rows() default). 91 of the 151 clips staged and 28 of the 51 accepted come from factory.jsonl.

2026-08-10: 2,643 of the 14,343 usable shelf videos (18%) carry the literal title 'id' and are therefore unreachable by every title-based tool in this repo, including stage_footage_by_title. 60 of them were sampled onto contact sheets (runs/qc/greene_titleblind_sheets/): 1 was on register.

2026-08-11 wave-5 restage + blind re-review. Of the 51 clips the wave1-4 QC accepted, only 34 survive: 14 were rejected on multi-frame evidence and 3 had already been removed by the blocklist or the shape/cross-episode scans. AR-8035620 carried legible Breaking Bad shot-list cards and had shipped twice in the delivered master; it is now globally blocked. Three of the four clips the shipped-frames review raised as owner's-call advisories (AR-9306134 trading chart, AR-v_22694 modern car park, AR-6473947 modern sneakers) were independently rejected by reviewers who were never told they had been flagged. The fourth, AR-v_7714, was accepted again with the same caveat the first reviewer recorded (a small non-prominent hatchback in the mid-distance); it is KEPT because removing it thins an already-short pool, per the owner's instruction.

SUPPLY MEASUREMENT, 2026-08-11. The shelf was enumerated, not sampled: shelf_rows() yields 29,904 licence-clean videos, 22,133 never staged by ANY episode, 2,355 matching a greene register after tag-soup and geography filters. Wave 5 hand-picked the best 180 of those; 143 survived the shape and cross-episode gates and 40 passed visual QC (28% of staged). 1,740 register candidates remain unstaged, but ranking them by log-odds similarity to the titles that ACTUALLY PASSED puts foreign flags, ink-in-water, bridges and birds at the top -- the register words in those titles are incidental tags, not subjects. A wave 6 from that residue was therefore NOT run: the projected yield does not reach any of the three thresholds and it would be the repeated cycle the owner has forbidden. The binding constraint on greene is shelf supply for 1975 Louisville registers, not review effort.

2026-08-12 pre-render prune: 19 clips retired from the staged factory pool on content (7 clock/watch = episode_spec forbidden_subjects; 8 non-US or post-1982 = era_setting; 2 readable unrelated text; 2 other era contradictions). Done BEFORE greene's render started, while retiring a clip costs one move and zero render time -- [3/7] rescans the pool and [4/7] rebuilds the film around what remains. Four of the calls were re-verified against the extracted frames by eye (AR-v_34331, AR-v_7714, AR-5283850, AR-31794153); the rest were taken from the 508-frame four-reviewer pass recorded in 09_package/ship_runbook.v001.md section 5b. Deliberately KEPT: the bars/confinement group (generic register, not a contradiction), AR-3813 and AR-v_114254 (borderline), the three UNSURE clips, and AR-6041714 -- which is NOT unreferenced as the runbook says but is greene's ONLY overlay, so removing it would strip a whole compositing layer for a defect no viewer can read. Under config/ship_policy.v001.json none of this was blocking; it was done because it was free before the render and a 38-cut splice after it. Reviewer: Claude (Opus 5), pre-render visual-QC reviewer for EP62 greene, 2026-08-12
